passages.head: প্রার্থনা কর — কাজ যেন নিষ্কাম হয়, বেশি কাজ যেন তাঁকে ভুলিয়ে না দেয়

passages.head: অফিসে, ব্যবসায় — সত্যে থাকো
passages.head_en: In the office or in business, hold to the truth

review.reason: Core image: work fully, mind at home in God
Clear, practical balance of work and God
Work is unavoidable; drop the craving for reward
Do what comes your way; don't pile on work
Work done rightly purifies the mind — encouraging
About charity as seva and ends "too hard for this age"; replaced by p11 (offer results to God)
Abstract one-liner; overlaps 06_i p12
Direct method for a worker: give gain/loss/joy/pain to God
For the overloaded: pray for selfless work, and less of it
Practical ethics for office/business work

review.ref: song:মন রে কৃষি কাজ জানো না
review.reason: Farming is a metaphor for sadhana; lyrics are not about work

problems.notes: Swapped an abstract/discouraging seva passage for practical ones: offering results, praying for less work, honesty at work; dropped off-topic song.

passages.head: অসুখে অধৈর্য? শিশুর মতো মায়ের উপর নির্ভর কর
passages.head_en: Impatient when ill? Lean on the Mother as a child does

passages.head: খুব অসুখ, কিন্তু রাতদিন ঈশ্বরীয় কথা
passages.head_en: Very ill, yet talking of God night and day

passages.head: শরীর দুদিনের — শক্তি চাইলে চেয়ো তাঁর নাম করার জন্য
passages.head_en: The body is brief; if you ask for strength, ask it to praise Him

songs: কর তাঁর নাম গান যতদিন দেহে রহে প্রাণ

review.reason: Whatever the body suffers, the devotee's inner wealth stays
Short, direct: mind on God puts pain aside
Models keeping God-talk alive through severe illness
Same skeleton prayer as 20_n p43, which opens with the teaching "body is brief, He alone is real"
Describes his own fading sense of "I" — not guidance for the reader
Past-karma framing can read as blame to an ill reader; p15 (pain comes with a body, even to the beloved) consoles instead
Specific to Keshab (illness caused by spiritual emotion); doesn't apply to the reader
Suffering is not a sign God has abandoned you
Body vs immortal soul — perspective for the seriously ill
Permission to be impatient; rely on the Mother like a child
How to pray when ill — strength in order to praise Him

problems.notes: Removed Thakur-/Keshab-specific states and a karma-as-cause passage; added consoling perspective and a model for praying when ill.

passages.head_en: Protect yourself — but don't harm them in return

passages.head_en: Listen to the elephant-driver's warning too

passages.head: বাঘনারায়ণকে দূর থেকে প্রণাম
passages.head_en: God is in the tiger too, but bow from afar

passages.head: নিন্দা? হাতি চলে যায়, ফিরেও চায় না
passages.head_en: Slandered? The elephant walks on without looking back

passages.head: কামারশালের নাই — সব সহ্য করবে
passages.head_en: Be like the blacksmith's anvil

passages.head: দুষ্ট লোকেরও দরকার আছে
passages.head_en: Even difficult people have their place

review.reason: Classic: don't bite, but hiss to protect yourself
Heed the warning; seeing God in all is no reason to stand in harm's way
Respect from a distance — a clear boundary
Bearing slander like the anvil
Understanding why such people exist
About the illumined beyond sin/virtue; to a reader being harmed it can read as "accept the beating"
Direct answer to "should I just keep quiet when harmed?"
For those mocked or slandered: walk on like the elephant

problems.notes: Dropped the passive "he who beat me feeds me" story; added the direct self-protection answer and the elephant image for slander.

passages.head_en: Like the tortoise, whose mind stays with its eggs

passages.head: রোজ তাঁকে ডাকা অভ্যাস করতে হয়
passages.head_en: Make calling on Him a daily habit

passages.head: মাঝে মাঝে নির্জনে গিয়ে ব্যাকুল হয়ে ডাকবে
passages.head_en: Now and then, go apart and call on Him

review.reason: Minimum practice for the very busy; hand Him the charge
Simple morning/evening practice for those without time
A busy woman whose mind stays on what matters
Live in the world, mind with God — like the tortoise
Daily habit builds longing — practical
Occasional solitude: realistic for householders

problems.notes: All six speak directly to the busy reader; song fits; no changes.

passages.head: বড়মানুষের বাড়ির ঝির মতো — সব কর, কিন্তু জেনো এ-সব তাঁর

passages.head_en: Compassion is not the same as attachment

passages.head_en: The silkworm trapped in the cocoon it built

passages.head: যাদের 'আমার আমার' করছ, চোখ বুজলেই নাই
passages.head_en: All you call 'mine' vanishes when your eyes close

songs: ভেবে দেখ মন কেউ কারু নয় মিছে ভ্রম ভূমণ্ডলে
এমনি মহামায়ার মায়া রেখেছ কি কুহক করে

review.reason: Camel image is apt but mocks grieving mothers and remarriage — harsh, no way forward
Nursemaid image only; 30_b p19 has the same image plus the instruction (all is His, I am His servant)
Compassion vs attachment — key distinction
Mudfish: live in it, shake it off
Silkworm: you could cut free if you chose
Impermanence of what we call "mine"
Fuller nursemaid teaching with the practical conclusion
The way forward: attachment falls away as devotion grows
Shift from "mine" to "Yours" — the core remedy

problems.notes: Page was diagnosis-heavy; added remedies (devotion loosens attachment, "Yours not mine") and dropped the harsh camel passage.
